dhcp-staff-full.done: The DHCP pool of the staff network in {site} is full.

test.power-led: Is the power LED on? Check plug and power strip.
test.ups-status: UPS display: on battery, overload or alarm?
test.mains-room: Do the lights and other sockets in the room work?
test.breaker: Fuse box: has a breaker tripped?
test.bypass: If the UPS itself is faulty: switch it to bypass or plug devices into the wall.
test.poe-port: Does the switch port still deliver PoE power?
test.link-led: Link LED lit on both ends of the cable?
test.cable-swap: Swap the patch cable or try another port.
test.port-status: Is the port up on the switch, in the right VLAN?
test.port-errors: Are the error counters on the port rising (CRC, drops)?
test.ap-led: Access point LED: on, blinking or dark?
test.wifi-client: Which access point is the device on, and how strong is the signal?
test.modem-led: Modem or fibre box: is the sync LED on?
test.ip-address: Does the device have an address from its network, not 169.254.x.x?
test.dhcp-leases: Firewall dashboard: how many addresses are left in the pool?
test.rogue-devices: Any unknown devices in the lease list, such as a private router?
test.dns-internal: Does the first internal DNS server answer?
test.dns-second: Does the second internal DNS server answer?
test.ping-device: Does the device answer a ping?
test.ping-loss: Packet loss or high latency over 50 pings?
test.wan-status: Firewall dashboard: which internet line is active?
test.ping-provider: Does a public address answer from the firewall?
test.speed-test: Speed test against the bandwidth in the contract.
test.isp-hotline: Check the provider's outage page, then call the business hotline with the contract number.
test.second-site: Does it work from another site? Then the problem is local.
test.tunnel-status: Tunnel status in the firewall dashboard: up or down, over which line?
test.ping-hq: Does the HQ firewall answer through the tunnel?
test.hq-reachable: Do other clinics lose their tunnel too? Then look at HQ.
test.dashboard-device: Is the device shown as online in the cloud dashboard?
test.firmware-version: Is the firmware current? Known bug in this version?
test.reboot-window: If needed, restart it after opening hours.
test.terminal-selftest: Run the connection test on the terminal.
test.print-queue: Print queue on the Mac: stopped or stuck jobs?
test.mdm-lastseen: MDM: when did the Mac last check in?
test.phone-registered: Phone display: registered with the telephone system?
test.vendor-contact: If the device itself is faulty: call the vendor service with serial number and error code.
test.vcenter-events: vCenter: events and alarms of the host or VM.
test.host-console: Out-of-band console of the host: power state, hardware errors?
test.vm-console: VM console: does the system boot, does the service start?
test.mlag-status: MLAG status on the remaining core switch: peer down, ports up?
test.ha-status: HA status of the firewall pair: which node is active?
test.storage-paths: Multipathing on the hosts: how many paths are active?
test.array-console: Storage array console: controller state and alarms?
test.service-port: Does the service answer on its port?
test.service-status: Service status on the server: since when are there errors in the log?
test.browser-warning: Does the browser show a certificate warning?
test.monitoring-cert: Why did certificate monitoring not warn in time?

switch-off.workaround: Plug the most important devices (reception Mac, card terminal) into the second switch or the spare switch.
switch-off.fix: Find out why it went off: power supply, UPS or defect. Replace it with the spare; the cloud template configures it.
switch-off.prevention: Switch on the UPS, a spare switch at HQ, and a monitoring alarm when a switch goes offline.

ap-off.workaround: Laptops roam to the next access point by themselves; where coverage is weak, move closer or use a cable.
ap-off.fix: Check the PoE port and cable. Replace the access point with the spare; it adopts the template.
ap-off.prevention: Overlapping coverage so one access point may fail, a spare in stock, and an offline alarm.

firewall-off.workaround: Nothing leaves the clinic: take card payments offline if the terminal allows it, otherwise cash; work locally.
firewall-off.fix: Check power and UPS. If it is defective, swap in the pre-configured spare from HQ.
firewall-off.prevention: Firewall on the UPS, a spare unit at HQ, and an HA pair for large clinics.

terminal-off.workaround: Use the second terminal, or cash or invoice.
terminal-off.fix: Check power and cable. If it is defective, the payment provider sends a replacement.
terminal-off.prevention: A spare terminal per region and a fixed port for each terminal.

printer-off.workaround: Print on another printer or hand the document over digitally.
printer-off.fix: Check power, cable, paper and labels; clear the print queue on the Mac.
printer-off.prevention: The same printer models everywhere, spare rolls in stock, fixed addresses.

mac-off.workaround: Work on another Mac: the data is in the cloud and on the file server, not on the Mac.
mac-off.fix: Check power and cable. If it is defective, MDM sets up a spare Mac in minutes.
mac-off.prevention: No local data, a spare Mac in stock, zero-touch enrolment.

phone-off.workaround: Forward calls to another phone or a mobile in the telephone system.
phone-off.fix: Check the PoE port and cable; replace the phone, it provisions itself.
phone-off.prevention: Phones on PoE behind the UPS, forwarding rules prepared.

medical-off.workaround: Use the device in another room or clinic; postpone or refer X-rays.
medical-off.fix: Check power and cable; call the vendor service with serial number and error code.
medical-off.prevention: A service contract with response time; vendor access only through the jump host.

mains-off.workaround: The network runs on the UPS for a while. Save work; payments may have to be cash.
mains-off.fix: Find the cause with the landlord or an electrician and reset the breakers.
mains-off.prevention: A UPS sized for the cabinet, monitored battery, and a plan for long outages.

ups-off.workaround: Put the devices straight on mains power (bypass).
ups-off.fix: Read the UPS display and log; replace the battery or the unit.
ups-off.prevention: Regular battery tests and replacement, UPS in monitoring.

host-off.workaround: Nothing to do: HA restarts the virtual servers on the other hosts within minutes.
host-off.fix: Check the hardware on the console, replace parts, bring the host back and let DRS rebalance.
host-off.prevention: Keep one host of reserve (N+1), test HA regularly, hardware support contract.

core-off.workaround: Nothing to do: every host and firewall is connected to both core switches.
core-off.fix: Check power and logs, replace the switch, restore the configuration from backup.
core-off.prevention: Keep the pair, test failover after changes, automate configuration backups.

hqfw-off.workaround: Nothing to do: the second node takes over the shared address.
hqfw-off.fix: Find the cause, repair or replace the node, and let the pair sync again.
hqfw-off.prevention: Test the HA failover twice a year; separate power feeds for both nodes.

storage-off.workaround: Nothing to do while the other half runs. Avoid changes until it is back.
storage-off.fix: Open a case with the vendor and replace the part.
storage-off.prevention: Support contract with fast parts delivery; path monitoring on every host.

isp-out.workaround: The backup line takes over automatically. Tell the team that things are slower.
isp-out.fix: Report the outage to the provider with the contract number and follow the ticket.
isp-out.prevention: Two providers on different media, both lines monitored, SLA document at hand.

vm-off.workaround: Start the virtual server again from vCenter.
vm-off.fix: Read the logs and find out why it stopped: update, full disk or crash.
vm-off.prevention: Monitoring of the service itself, not just a ping.

external-out.workaround: Use the documented fallback (paper form, cash) until the provider is back.
external-out.fix: Nothing to fix on our side; follow the provider's status page.
external-out.prevention: A fallback procedure for every external service in the clinic handbook.

device-off.workaround: Use another device of the same kind.
device-off.fix: Check power and cable; replace it if it is defective.
device-off.prevention: Standard models and spare parts in stock.

slow-device.workaround: Restart the device outside opening hours.
slow-device.fix: Check firmware and error counters; update or replace it.
slow-device.prevention: Monitor latency and errors; roll out firmware in stages.

tunnels-down.workaround: Everything in the cloud keeps working. Keep X-ray images on the device until the tunnel is back.
tunnels-down.fix: Check the tunnel in the dashboard (keys, addresses, firmware) and restart it.
tunnels-down.prevention: Alarm on tunnel state, a tested template, no manual changes.

dhcp-full.workaround: Give one important Mac a temporary fixed address.
dhcp-full.fix: Find what used up the pool (unknown devices?), then enlarge the pool or shorten the lease time.
dhcp-full.prevention: Alarm at 80 % pool use; unknown devices are not allowed on the staff network.

dhcp-guest-full.workaround: Tell guests the Wi-Fi is full for a moment; the team is not affected.
dhcp-guest-full.fix: Shorten the lease time on the guest network, for example to one hour.
dhcp-guest-full.prevention: Short leases and a pool large enough for a full waiting room.

dns-stopped.workaround: As long as one server answers, nothing to do. If both fail, restart the service on one of them.
dns-stopped.fix: Read the logs, repair the service and check the zone data.
dns-stopped.prevention: Two servers on different hosts (anti-affinity) and DNS monitoring per server.

cert-expired.workaround: Do not click through warnings on medical systems; issue a new certificate right away.
cert-expired.fix: Renew the certificate and install it on the server.
cert-expired.prevention: Automatic renewal and an expiry alarm 30 and 14 days ahead.

wan-cut.workaround: The backup line takes over. Avoid large uploads until the main line is back.
wan-cut.fix: Report it to the provider and check the cable inside the building.
wan-cut.prevention: LTE backup in every clinic and monitoring of both lines.

wifi-cut.workaround: Move closer to an access point or use a cable.
wifi-cut.fix: Check the device's Wi-Fi settings; push the Wi-Fi profile again via MDM.
wifi-cut.prevention: Wi-Fi profiles from MDM and a coverage measurement in every room.

storage-cut.workaround: Nothing to do: the second path takes over.
storage-cut.fix: Replace the cable or transceiver and check the port.
storage-cut.prevention: Two paths per host and path monitoring.

lan-cut.workaround: Use another port or another cable.
lan-cut.fix: Replace the cable; check the wall socket and the patch panel.
lan-cut.prevention: Labelled cabling and spare patch cables in the cabinet.

slow-wan.workaround: Postpone large uploads; switch to the backup line by hand if needed.
slow-wan.fix: Measure, then report to the provider with the measurements.
slow-wan.prevention: Monitor latency and loss; an SLA with defined quality.

slow-link.fix: Replace the cable and check the speed and duplex settings.
slow-link.prevention: Monitor the error counters of the ports.

tunnel-cut.workaround: The second tunnel takes over if its line works.
tunnel-cut.fix: Check the tunnel in the dashboard and restart it.
tunnel-cut.prevention: Two tunnels over two lines and an alarm on tunnel state.

scenario.offline: Hamburg: fibre and LTE both gone
scenario.guest-pool: Full waiting room in Berlin: guest Wi-Fi out of addresses
scenario.access-point: Berlin: Wi-Fi in treatment room 1 gone
scenario.dns-both: Both DNS servers at HQ stop

event.vmRestarted: HA restarts {count} virtual servers on the other hosts: {devices}. Short interruption.
event.vmDownCapacity: Not enough memory left in the cluster: {devices} stay off.
event.vmDownStorage: No host reaches the storage: {devices} stop.
event.vmDownHost: No host is left to run {devices}.
event.wanFailover: {sites} switch to the backup internet line.
event.vpnFailover: The VPN tunnel of {sites} comes back over the backup line.
event.vpnDown: {sites} lose the VPN tunnel to headquarters.
event.serviceDegraded: For {site}, these are slow or briefly interrupted: {services}.

warning.redundancyLost: Redundancy lost: {devices} is out, its partner now carries everything alone.
warning.capacityReserveUsed: The cluster reserve is used up ({devices} out). Another host failure would not be absorbed.
warning.onBattery: {device} runs on battery. Plan for the moment it runs empty.
warning.serviceRedundancyLost: {service} has only one server left ({devices} out).

outcome.healthy: Everything works. Pick a scenario, or choose a device on the map and break something.
outcome.absorbed: Nobody notices: redundancy takes over. A safety margin is gone, though.
outcome.degraded: Everything still works, but slower or after a short interruption.

cap.authenticate-users: User login on the file server
cap.forward-results: Lab results to the practice software
